newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan militia says it takes provincial capital.
newsitem.headline: Afghan militia says it takes provincial capital.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia said it had captured the Parwan province capital of Charikar north of Kabul on Saturday, driving out the forces of ousted President Burhanuddin Rabbani, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service reported.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted Taleban sources as saying the militia forces were now heading further north towards the ousted government's military base of Jabal-us-Seraj. There was no immediate independent confirmation of the report.
Taleban sources had earlier said they believed Rabbani and his aides fled to Jabal-us-Seraj before the militia captured the national capital Kabul and set up a new government there on Friday.

A statement issued by Rabbani on Friday said his administration had transferred its headquarters from Kabul to Parwan and the adjoining Kapisa province and was "carrying out, among other tasks, security and defence affairs" from there.
AIP quoted Taleban sources as saying at least 18 pro-Rabbani fighters were killed and several captured in the Charikar fighting, compared to only five Taleban men killed.
